messages:
Alex H.: hey team, handing over now for the evening shift :wave:. Quick summary up top — we had a routing fallback cascade between 16:10-16:28 UTC that caused elevated p95 and a ~3% 429 rate for hosted inference (mostly short chats). Root cause appears to be an nginx upstream healthcheck flapping after a recent config push to routing rules.

Alex H.: timeline: 16:08 deploy (routing weights tweak) -> 16:10 error spike starts -> 16:12 autoscaler reacted -> 16:14 fallback to cheaper model variant triggered -> 16:25 manual mitigation (reverted weight) -> 16:28 errors subsiding. Customer impact: intermittent 429s and higher latency for <10k active keys; no data loss, but some small customers saw failed requests and UX retries.

ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: #INC-2026-321 routing-fallback-elevated-429s (severity: S2)

Riley S.: thanks alex. current status?

Alex H.: current state: stable-ish. p95 back to baseline, 429 rate down to 0.2% (from 3%). Autoscaler paused pending follow-up (we disabled scale-up to avoid oscillation). We left two remediation flags in the console: revert routing weights (done), disable aggressive healthcheck probing (WIP).

Samir K.: did we hit any quota limits or internal throttles?

Alex H.: quick check: no token/plan quota hits. Bottleneck was routing table churn + healthcheck timeouts causing upstreams to be marked unhealthy. That made router fall back to lower-capacity pools -> higher latency -> 429s as queue filled. No GPU OOMs.

Riley S.: who is primary/secondary for the next 12h window?

Alex H.: primary: Riley S. (you already), secondary: Samir K. After-hours backup: @on-call-rotation (pagerduty). Please escalate to Eng-Platform if we see >1% sustained 429s for >15m.

Riley S.: noted — I'll be primary. coverage gap?

Alex H.: small gap: we don't have a dedicated infra person on-call for the 22:00-00:00 UTC window (scheduled as on-call-rotation). If an infra-level kernel/gke node issue shows up we may be slow to respond. Action: Riley, please ping infra on Slack if you see cluster node flapping. I left a runbook pointer: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/routing-fallback — contains mitigations and the exact nginx flag to revert.

Samir K.: can you paste the revert command here so I have it in the thread?

Alex H.: sure — the quick revert we used:

```
# revert routing weight tweak
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/weights -d '{"route":"chat","weight":{...}}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRLPLANE_TOKEN"
# then restart nginx on the affected router nodes
kubectl rollout restart deployment/router -n inference
```

Alex H.: note: limited rollout first (3 nodes) then monitor. We also lowered healthcheck aggressiveness:

```
# set healthcheck timeout
kubectl patch cm router-config -n inference --patch '{"data":{"healthcheck_timeout":"5s"}}'
```

Riley S.: good. Any customer followups required?

Alex H.: yes — flagged two customers (acct ids: acct-772, acct-981) who reported errors. Support ticket numbers: SUP-12455, SUP-12457. SRE suggested proactive email for high-usage customers in the affected timeslot. I've logged a short post-incident note in the incident doc: https://internal.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-321/notes

ops-bot: PAGE sent to on-call rotation: Riley S. (primary), Samir K. (secondary)

Riley S.: I'll take ownership of the follow-up. Immediate next steps for me: 1) watch 429 rate for 30m, 2) validate autoscaler config (avoid oscillation), 3) confirm infra coverage for 22:00-00:00 UTC by pinging infra channel at 17:05 UTC.

Samir K.: I'll audit autoscaler logs and leave any config diffs under the incident doc. If I see oscillation traces I'll revert to the safe profile (profile-id: safe-v1).

Alex H.: outstanding follow-ups for the next shift (in order):
- Riley: monitor, confirm infra ping, update SUP tickets with root cause summary.
- Samir: autoscaler audit + config PR if needed (link it in the incident doc).
- Riley/Samir: schedule a short postmortem call tomorrow 09:30 UTC if incident is stable.

Riley S.: got it. One more thing — we should add a small automated guard to prevent routing weight changes from auto-applying if upstream health is unstable. I'll open a ticket: ENG-PLAT-1543.

Alex H.: thanks. I'm leaving the pager with you. If anything degrades back to >1% 429s escalate immediately and invoke the fallback playbook.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: Pager duty handoff logged. Next on-call rotation: Riley S. (primary) until 2026-03-15 04:00 UTC.

Riley S.: thanks alex. handing over now — logging this thread as the official handover note. :thumbsup:

Samir K.: good handover, thanks all. I'll be around for the audit step.
